entities.summary: Alfred Thompson Denning, Baron Denning,, was an English barrister and judge. He was called to the Bar of England and Wales in 1923 and became a King's Counsel in 1938. Denning became a judge in 1944 when he was appointed to the Probate, Divorce and Admiralty Division of the High Court of Justice, and transferred to the King's Bench Division in 1945. He was made a Lord Justice of Appeal in 1948 after less than five years in the High Court. He became a Lord of Appeal in Ordinary in 1957 and after five years in the House of Lords returned to the Court of Appeal as Master of the Rolls in 1962, a position he held for twenty years.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the development of English law and a prominent judge during World War II, Baron Denning played a crucial role in shaping the country's legal landscape. His appointment as Master of the Rolls in 1962 had a lasting impact on the Court of Appeal, influencing its procedures and precedents for decades.
